findings.issue_text: **1. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-62` — team admin authorization check is unreachable; any accepted member can install team-wide credentials**
**2. `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96` — `prisma` is not imported**
**3. `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97` — the Zod `safeParse` wrapper is persisted as the credential key**
**5. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14` — the credential-sync request carries no authentication**
**6. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11` — `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not do what the comments say**
**7. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27` — writes the literal string `"refresh_token"` as a refresh token**

`hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-199` — `hubspotRefreshToken` is a `Response`, so `.expiresIn` is `undefined` → `expiryDate` becomes `NaN`, then `prisma.credential.update({ key: hubspotRefreshToken as any })` serializes a `Response` (effectively `{}`) over the user's credential, destroying it. The surrounding `try/catch` swallows the follow-on `setAccessToken(undefined)`, so this fails silently.

`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:92-93` — `res?.data` is `undefined` on a `Response`, so `token.access_token` throws a `TypeError`; the catch sees a message that isn't `invalid_grant` and returns the auth object with the stale token, i.e. refresh silently no-ops forever.

`webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:87-90`, `office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:77`, `larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:88-98`, and `hubspot` all received `refreshOAuthTokens` but still validate with their strict provider-specific schemas. Webex's `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` requires `refresh_token`, `refresh_token_expires_in`, and a `z.literal` scope — none of which a minimal sync response has, so it rejects with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Lark reads `data.data.refresh_expires_in` and writes `undefined` into the credential. The feature is therefore only half-implemented: enabling credential sync breaks four of the seven apps it was wired into. Either route these through `parseRefreshTokenResponse` too, or document explicitly which apps support sync.
**10. `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-104` — refresh is unconditional, and the refreshed token is then discarded**

There is no expiry check. `getClient` runs on every `SalesforceCalendarService` construction, so **every** booking operation performs a full token refresh round-trip against Salesforce. This will hit Salesforce's OAuth rate limits under load and adds latency to every call.

The new token is written to the DB (line 96-99) but `new jsforce.Connection` on line 101 still passes `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` — the **old** value. The refresh is pure overhead; the connection uses the token that was just superseded.
It bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens` entirely, so Salesforce is the one app that ignores the credential-sync endpoint this PR exists to add — directly contrary to the PR intent.
Line 31: `.parse()` on an untrusted body throws a `ZodError` out of the handler → Next returns a 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400. Use `safeParse` and return 400 with the issue list.

Lines 24-29: `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset and the header is absent, this is `undefined !== undefined` → `false` → the check **passes**. This is only saved if `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is itself derived from the secret being set — which I could not verify in this checkout. Add an explicit `if (!process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET) return 500` and use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for the comparison.
No `req.method` guard: a `GET` reaches the body parse and 500s. Reject non-POST with 405.
Line 62-64: `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is unguarded — a bad ciphertext or wrong key throws and returns 500 rather than 400.
Line 34: `prisma.user.findUnique` selects every user column (including the password hash) just to test existence. Add `select: { id: true }`.
**13. `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-264` — diagnostics removed and behavior changed from degrade to throw**

**14. `decodeOAuthState.ts:10` / `encodeOAuthState.ts:9` — unguarded `JSON.parse` on user-controlled input.** `req.query.state` comes back from the OAuth provider; a malformed value throws out of every callback handler as a 500. Wrap in try/catch and return `undefined`, and validate the result with a Zod schema rather than an unchecked `as IntegrationOAuthCallbackState` cast — the type assertion gives false confidence that `teamId` is a number, which matters given issue #1.

**16. `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17` — hardcoded slug replacing `appConfig.slug`.** This moves away from the single source of truth used two lines above (`getAppKeysFromSlug(appConfig.slug)`) and on line 22 (`appConfig.scope`). If the slug ever changes, keys resolve from one place and the redirect URI from another. Revert to the template literal.

**17. `createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42,45` — unused select and wrong error type.** `members: { select: { userId: true } }` is fetched and never read. `throw new Error("User does not belong to the team")` produces a 500; it should be `new HttpError({ statusCode: 403, ... })` like the 401 above it. (Both disappear if #1 is fixed as suggested.)

**18. Duplicated feature-flag expression.** `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` appears in both `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15` and `refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5`. If these ever drift, parsing and fetching disagree about which mode they're in. Export a single `credentialSyncingEnabled` constant.

**19. `refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8` — no status check on the sync response.** A 500 from the sync endpoint is returned to callers as a `Response` and only fails later, in provider-specific error handling, with a misleading message.
**20. `app-credential.ts:21` — stray empty `/** */` JSDoc.** Either document the handler or remove it. Similarly `app-credential.ts:54` has a comment with stray leading whitespace.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **5. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14` — the credential-sync request carries no authentication**

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, the code does a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no auth material (no Authorization header, no shared secret, no signature, no token, etc.). The only data sent is `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`. So the finding that the credential-sync request carries no authentication is directly verifiable from the diff and is a reasonable security concern (it relies entirely on external/network-side protection of that endpoint).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **6. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11` — `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not do what the comments say**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, the object literal uses computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`. That expression is evaluated once at definition time to a single string (e.g., something like "[object Object]"/"ZodString"), not “any property”. So it does not implement “assume any property with a number is the expiry” nor “allow other properties”. It effectively defines one fixed property key (and the second computed key likely overwrites the first), meaning the schema won’t accept arbitrary numeric/unknown token fields as the comments imply.

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is handled as `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""));` with no try/catch. If `reqBody.keys` is invalid ciphertext, the env key is wrong/empty, or the decrypted plaintext is not valid JSON, either `symmetricDecrypt(...)` or `JSON.parse(...)` will throw. There is no error handling to convert this into a controlled 4xx response, so the exception will bubble up and Next.js will return a 500.

This is more of a potential optimization/minimization suggestion than a definite problem proven by the diff.
